Sure! Here’s a simple yet flavorful way to make an **Indian‑style grilled steak** with a quick tandoori‑inspired rub and a creamy yogurt sauce. Feel free to adjust spice levels to your taste. --- ## Ingredients | Item | Quantity | |------|----------| | Ribeye or sirloin steak (1–1.5 lb) | 1 piece | | Plain Greek yogurt | ½ cup | | Lemon juice | 2 Tbsp | | Garlic paste | 1 Tbsp | | Ginger paste | 1 Tbsp | | Ground cumin | 1 tsp | | Ground coriander | 1 tsp | | Garam masala | ½ tsp | | Turmeric powder | ¼ tsp | | Paprika or Kashmiri red chili powder | 1 tsp (adjust for heat) | | Salt | ½ tsp | | Fresh cilantro, chopped | 2 Tbsp | | Olive oil or melted butter | 1 Tbsp | | Optional: crushed roasted cumin seeds | 1 tsp | ### For the finishing sauce (optional) | Item | Quantity | |------|----------| | Heavy cream or coconut milk | ¼ cup | | Butter | 1 Tbsp | | Fresh mint leaves, finely chopped | 1 Tbsp | | Lime wedges | for serving | | Extra fresh cilantro | for garnish | --- ## Instructions ### 1. Prepare the Marinade 1. In a bowl, whisk together: - Yogurt, lemon juice, garlic paste, ginger paste, - Cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, paprika, - Salt, olive oil/melted butter, and optional roasted cumin. 2. Taste and adjust salt or spices if needed. ### 2. Marinate the Steak 1. Pat the steak dry with paper towels. 2. Coat both sides generously with the yogurt mixture; you can use a brush or your hands (wear gloves). 3. Cover and refrigerate for at least **30 minutes** (up to 4 hours). Longer marination deepens flavor but isn’t mandatory. ### 3. Preheat Your Grill or Skillet - **Grill:** Heat to high (medium‑high for thicker cuts). Oil the grates lightly. - **Skillet/Griddle:** Use cast iron or stainless steel; preheat over medium‑high until it starts smoking slightly. ### 4. Cook the Steak | Step | Details | |------|---------| | **Sear** | Place steak on grill/skillet. Sear each side for 2–3 min to get a nice crust. | | **Finish** | Reduce heat to medium. Continue cooking to your preferred doneness:
• Rare: 120–125 °F (48–52 °C)
• Medium‑rare: 130–135 °F (54–57 °C)
• Medium: 140–145 °F (60–63 °C)
Use a meat thermometer for accuracy. | | **Rest** | Remove steak, tent loosely with foil, and let rest 5–7 min. This redistributes juices. | ### 5. Optional Creamy Mint Sauce 1. While steak rests, melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat. 2. Add heavy cream/coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer. 3. Stir in chopped mint, season with salt, and simmer for 2–3 min until slightly thickened. 4. Keep warm until serving. ### 6. Plate & Serve 1. Slice steak against the grain into thin strips. 2. Drizzle or spoon the mint‑cream sauce over slices. 3. Garnish with extra cilantro and serve with lime wedges on the side. 4. Pair with naan, basmati rice, or a fresh cucumber raita for a complete meal. --- ## Tips & Variations - **Spice Level:** If you prefer milder flavors, reduce paprika or omit the chili powder. For more heat, add cayenne or fresh chopped green chilies to the yogurt mix. - **Flavor Boost:** Sprinkle a pinch of smoked paprika or a few drops of liquid smoke during searing for a smoky undertone. - **Vegetarian Alternative:** Swap steak for paneer cubes or tofu, marinating them similarly before grilling. - **Serving Idea:** Toss sliced steak with a quick salad of diced tomatoes, onions, cucumbers, and a squeeze of lime for a refreshing contrast. Enjoy your homemade Indian‑style steak—rich, aromatic, and surprisingly easy to pull off!
